preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 5000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n for n, s in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if n.isdigit() and s)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 5000) and the second line is a string s of length n consisting of lowercase Latin letters.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 5000 for n in (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[::2]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the length n of the string s satisfies 1 ≤ n ≤ 5000.

preconditions.expression: all(s.islower() and s.isalpha() for s in stdin.splitlines()[1::2])
preconditions.description: Each string s consists only of lowercase Latin letters.

postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly 2t lines, where t is the number of test cases.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout_lines[i * 2]) == n and len(stdout_lines[i * 2 + 1]) == 1 for i in range(t) for n in [int(stdin.splitlines()[i * 2 + 1])])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the first output line is the lexicographically smallest string s' of length n, and the second line is the smallest k (1 ≤ k ≤ n) that achieves it.

postconditions.expression: all(s_prime == min((transform(s, k) for k in range(1, n + 1)), key=lambda x: (x, k))[0] for i, (n, s) in enumerate(zip((int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[::2]), stdin.splitlines()[1::2])) for s_prime in [stdout_lines[i * 2]])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string s' is the lexicographically smallest string achievable by any k in 1..n. If multiple k's yield the same s', the smallest k is chosen.

postconditions.expression: all(k == min(k for k in range(1, n + 1) if transform(s, k) == s_prime) for i, (n, s) in enumerate(zip((int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[::2]), stdin.splitlines()[1::2])) for s_prime, k in zip(stdout_lines[i * 2::2], stdout_lines[i * 2 + 1::2]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output k is the smallest integer in 1..n that produces the lexicographically smallest string s'.
